legend: After winning a hard-fought battle against Ogre Magi, Thrall returned to his manufactory in upland Druud to repair his stormcrafting device. He was tinkering around with the plates of a faulty circular parallel plate capacitor that he retrieved from the heart of the device. Both of the circular plates have a uniform radius of r%%ZSMJ0%% units. Thrall wanted to control the distance d%%ZSMJ1%% between the two plates, and so he decided to join them by soldering many equally spaced strings of length L%%ZSMJ2%%. One end of each string was soldered to the side of the +ve%%ZSMJ3%% plate, while the other end was soldered to the side of the −ve%%ZSMJ4%% plate.
Figure 1: Salvaging the spoils of war.
This contraption enabled him to rotate one of the circular plates (say, the +ve%%ZSMJ5%% plate) and consequently calibrate the value of d%%ZSMJ6%%.
Figure 2: Rotating the +ve%%ZSMJ10%% plate by different angles (θ%%ZSMJ11%%).
If Thrall rotates the +ve%%ZSMJ12%% circular plate by an angle of θ%%ZSMJ13%% degrees, what would be the corresponding value of d%%ZSMJ14%%, the distance between the circular plates?
input: The first line contains an integer t%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤t≤100)%%ZSMJ16%% — the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of a single line containing three space-separated integers r%%ZSMJ17%% (0<r≤109)%%ZSMJ18%%, L%%ZSMJ19%% (0<L≤109)%%ZSMJ20%%, and θ%%ZSMJ21%% (0∘<θ∘<180∘)%%ZSMJ22%% — the radius of the plates, the length of the strings, and the angle (in degrees) by which Thrall rotates the +ve%%ZSMJ23%% plate respectively.

It is guaranteed that for all test cases, the string length L%%ZSMJ24%% is sufficient to allow the rotation of the +ve%%ZSMJ25%% plate by θ%%ZSMJ26%% degrees, resulting in a real and non-negative value of d%%ZSMJ27%%.
output: For each test case, output a single number d%%ZSMJ28%% in a line — the distance between the circular plates.
The answer will be considered correct if the absolute error does not exceed 10−6%%ZSMJ29%%.
